correctness.rationale: The exact corner-triangle geometric decomposition holds whenever all polygon edges receive a sample. The exact joint survival integral proves the explicit expectation surrogate, and the probability of missing an edge is exponentially small. Joint scaled endpoint gaps converge to independent exponential variables and possess uniform moment bounds; all moment limits and the variance follow. A positive-definite Hessian proves strictly convex edge-allocation cost and uniqueness; the cyclic stationarity conditions give odd/even equality rigidity, and the closed quadrilateral edge equations force a parallelogram. Standalone geometric, moment, numerical and Monte Carlo checks passed; finite checks are only supporting evidence.

value.rationale: The theorem determines a canonical affine-invariant probability allocation for a natural random-inscribed-polygon area loss, not just a renaming of the usual arclength law. Its exact independent corner-product distribution determines fluctuations; equal-weight optimality has an unexpected odd/even algebraic classification and full parallelogram rigidity among convex quadrilaterals. For a long rectangle, optimized allocation improves the leading asymptotic mean error over perimeter-uniform sampling by an unbounded factor (a+b)^2/(4ab), giving clear mathematical and sampling-design motivation.
